paragraphs.text: Few warriors dare to challenge a knight of Capashen. Should one do so, there is one fewer.
Benalia has no need for peacocks to serve as symbols of vanity. The Capashens strut more proudly than any bird.
Their shields are Benalia's outermost battlements.
"You lived for Serra's love. Will you not die for it?"
The best defense is to not get hit.
Commanders order soldiers to attack. Field surgeons order them to heal. Both are obeyed without question.
Who is truer: you who are, or you who are to be?
The archangels zealously drove Serra's light into every corner of their new home as if their creator still commanded them.
Behind his eyes is the pain of every soldier his hands have healed.
A thing of Serra's realm exists only by the grace of her followers' faith.
Treasures, trinkets, trash—the relics of the past are brought forth again.
"To forgive our enemies is to forgive ourselves."
An angel's touch can prepare a soldier for battle more than a thousand military drills.
Their commitment to Serra is as solid as any shield.
Poorly trained griffins sometimes attack the noble audiences that gather to watch their progress.
Falling from heaven is not as painful as surviving the impact.
"Next to Law is Duty, and Duty must be obeyed. If the frame of Duty is broken, none shall weave life's fabric." —*Song of All*, canto 167
"Next to Grace is Reason, and Reason must be retained. If the web of Reason comes unwoven, madness will escape." —*Song of All*, canto 167
The blinding barrier served Benalia better than a hundred shields.
Illusion steals reality from the unwise.
Students who had seen Rayne argue with Urza were certain she had summoned it to make him seem warmer by comparison.
"Chancellor Rayne canceled the annual beeble roast. I should have married a crueler woman." —Barrin
If at first you don't succeed, run away and hide.
Campus pranksters initiate new students with the old "beeble bomb" routine.
"Mind if I just lie down right here for a few weeks?"
It isn't truly born until its first flight.
For a moment, Urza thought not of war and destruction, but of the freedom of the skies.
It's tastiest when served with the fish it stole.
Barrin drowned his doubts about Urza's project by delving ever deeper into its details.
If the eyes are windows to the soul, their souls are not of this world.
Just as Serra crafted angels of light and faith, Urza constructed an army of sorcery and power to resist the coming invasion.
"Urza says he's sane. Perhaps, but measures of sanity among planeswalkers are hard to come by." —Barrin
"Urza, I've discovered more promising students than you and my husband have, combined. And I haven't lost a single one." —Rayne, Academy Chancellor
Arrows are only one way to remove an enemy.
"Do try to keep an open mind, would you?"
"Of course she's at the head of her class. All her classmates have disappeared." —Gatha, Tolarian renegade
Rayne once made several unkind comparisons between the bird's naked opportunism and Urza's.
"The academy educates; I employ. It's a perfect arrangement." —Gatha, Tolarian renegade
"I will trade life for life with the insurgents. Our resources, unlike theirs, are limitless." —Davvol, Evincar of Rath
The muck claims a hundred living things for each meager treasure it spews forth.
"'Davvol, blast those elves.' 'Davvol, transport those troops.' No one cares that today is my birthday."
Many sent to serve Davvol carried such instruments, as if to remind him who their true masters were.
Rath is a disease all its inhabitants carry.
This is a world of spiteful wasps that sting and kill even as they die.
"The rate of spread in this region is unacceptable. Start again." —Davvol, Evincar of Rath
Often it's not the hunter or the hunted but the opportunist who thrives in Rath.
Being one would be an honor, if the word "honor" had any meaning in Phyrexia.
They exist to cease.
They're not just retrievers, they're carriers.
The grave robbers arrived the day after the burial. They were a day too late.
"For all the priceless tomes they have destroyed, one would think they would taste better." —Davvol, Evincar of Rath
"This monstrosity will do—for now." —Davvol, Evincar of Rath
Davvol encouraged the skirges; they made excellent sentries and were quite edible if properly seasoned.
As no one has ever accepted a second invitation to Davvol's table, the evincar often dines alone.
Only the coldest hearts and the strongest stomachs can stand against it.
Gatha showed remarkable prowess in increasing his subjects' stature. Their lifespans, however, were another matter.
He craves only one commodity.
When Gatha fell, he was called to account for each abomination he created.
After their first encounter, the goblins named him Chuck.
A steed grows with its rider.
Gatha survived as long as he did by giving all Keld's predators exactly what they wanted.
Did the land make the Keldons? Did the Keldons make the land? Or were they simply meant for each other?
Goblins don't know the meaning of the word "tactics" —or the word "meaning," for that matter.
"What are we celebratin' again?"
"Grow food in dirt? Save time—eat dirt."
"Goblins build with true zeal—and anything else within arm's reach."
"The Keldons' ogre campaign provided more body parts than my meager facility could properly use." —Gatha, Tolarian renegade
Ask a Keldon to hold his temper and you'll be left holding your guts.
Keldons divide all their spoils into two groups: trophies and catapult ammunition.
Sometimes the mountain takes. —Keldon saying
Many Keldon warriors bear the mark of intentional insanity.
The climax of a warlord's career is always death.
Not all Keld's warriors are found on the battlefield.
Keldon warriors don't need signals to tell them when to attack, but when to stop.
Land charred black, rivers boiled, Crops and wells alike despoiled, Mountains leveled, forests felled— Footprints of the beasts of Keld.
You'll never get a Keldon's goat.
The Phyrexian killing machines couldn't have known the seriousness of their mistake in wounding the ape—they'd never seen it angry.
A fruit must rot before its seed can sprout. —Yavimaya saying
Like a masterful quilter, Yavimaya stitches together patches of color to warn its denizens of threats.
From Gaea grew the world, and the world was silent. From Gaea grew the world's elves, and the world was silent no more. —Elvish teaching
The king of Yavimaya's waters pays constant attention to his subjects . . . and thrives on their adulation.
The balance of nature dictates that one day humans will be stepped on by bugs.
"In Llanowar, we tend the forest's boughs and branches. In Yavimaya, we are a part of them." —Rofellos of Llanowar
The seed torches' pollen gives off light, but the elves find it heightens their senses as well.
In case of emergency, crush bug.
"This is my place of power. Nothing can take root here unless I allow it." —Multani, maro-sorcerer
Most spiders wait patiently for their prey to arrive. Most spiders aren't forty feet tall.
To renew the land, plow the land. To destroy the land, do nothing. —Druids' saying
"Rise, elf. We are both of Gaea, and thus we are equal." —Multani, to Rofellos
Much to Multani's chagrin, Rofellos gleefully tutored Yavimaya's elves on the rudest and most vulgar words spoken in Llanowar.
Rain from this storm leaves you pinned to the ground like an insect.
From each seed, a world. From each world, a thousand seeds.
"I think it no accident that every civilized people has discovered the art of distillation." —Rofellos of Llanowar
The students disliked the secretary for its unfailing memory—until they discovered it couldn't dodge thrown objects.
Toward the end, Gatha struggled to keep his experiments in and his patrons out.
As the invasion drew closer, Urza's means began to resemble Phyrexia's end.
Step 1: Find your cousin. Step 2: Get your cousin in the cannon. Step 3: Find another cousin.
Garbage in, treasure out.
Tawnos left a legacy of animal designs in many of Urza's creations.
"At this rate I fully expect to be replaced by a clockwork golem by year's end." —Barrin
Urza's metathran children were conceived, birthed, and nurtured by an integrated system of machines.
"What we do not use up, we use again." —Urza
Karn felt more secure about his value to Urza when he realized he didn't need regular trimming.
"Stop thinking like an artificer, Urza, and start thinking like a father!" —Rayne, Academy Chancellor
For all its traps and defenses, Yavimaya has its havens, too.
